title: JEPAMatch: Geometric Representation Shaping for Semi-Supervised Learning
abstract: arXiv:2604.21046v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Semi-supervised learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for leveraging large amounts of unlabeled data to improve the performance of machine learning models when labeled data are scarce. Among existing approaches, methods derived from FixMatch have achieved state-of-the-art results in image classification by combining weak and strong data augmentations with confidence-based pseudo-labeling. Despite their strong empirical performance, these methods typically struggle with two critical bottlenecks: majority classes tend to dominate the learning process, which is amplified by incorrect pseudo-labels, leading to biased models. Furthermore, noisy early pseudo-labels prevent the model from forming clear decision boundaries, requiring prolonged training to learn informative representation. In this paper, we introduce a paradigm shift from conventional logical output threshold base, toward an explicit shaping of geometric representations

translated_title: JEPAMatch：半监督学习的几何表示塑造
translated_abstract: 半监督学习已成为一种强大的范式，可在标注数据稀缺时利用大量未标注数据来提升机器学习模型的性能。在现有方法中，源自FixMatch的方法通过结合弱增强和强增强以及基于置信度的伪标签，在图像分类中取得了最先进的结果。尽管这些方法具有强大的实证性能，但它们通常面临两个关键瓶颈：多数类倾向于主导学习过程，而错误的伪标签会加剧这一现象，导致模型产生偏差。此外，早期噪声伪标签阻碍了模型形成清晰的决策边界，需要长时间训练才能学习到信息丰富的表示。在本文中，我们引入了一种范式转变，从传统的逻辑输出阈值基础转向对几何表示的显式塑造。
tldr: 本文提出JEPAMatch方法，通过显式塑造几何表示而非依赖逻辑输出阈值，解决了半监督学习中多数类主导和早期噪声伪标签导致的偏差与决策边界模糊问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes JEPAMatch, which explicitly shapes geometric representations instead of relying on logical output thresholds, addressing issues of majority class dominance and noisy early pseudo-labels that cause bias and unclear decision boundaries in semi-supervised learning.
